All instructional people I've seen online say that you should focus on the front sight of your firearm when aiming with both eyes open. This seems strange to me, because that makes the target blurry and hard to see. I find it much easier to instead focus on the target and let my front sight instead become slightly blurry, especially when shooting a target that's further away. However, I hardly think I would know better than all of the experts, so I think I'm missing something. Why should you focus on the front sight instead of the target when shooting with both eyes open?
Why should you focus on the front sight when shooting with both eyes open?
Basically it is more important to clearly see the alignment of your sights than it is to see the target. Doesn't matter what you want to hit, if your sights aren't aligned you won't hit it.

It's easier to get used to ignoring the unused eyes input than to strain to hold one eyelid closed. When focusing on the target, get the back sight centered in your vision, then if you can hold your head immobile to the stock you don't have to worry about it. Then alternate focus between the target and front sight, and when you start to squeeze you'll know where in that blur that is the target to aim the sharply focused front sight on. Source.
